points.text: Method-level novelty limited; loss, aggregation, distillation taken from DepthFL
'First' layerwise QFL claim lacks experimental comparison to eSQFL
Self-built Q-HeteroFL baseline appears under-tuned, high variance, collapses
Headline 12.4% gain is relative only to self-built baseline
Missing stronger natural baselines (shared sub-circuit FedAvg, per-depth groups, no-KD variant)
Unfair comparison: Quorus uses ensemble of per-layer classifiers, baselines single output
Gains over Standalone/Vanilla QFL small, within std, sometimes negative
No statistical significance testing behind best-result markings
Very small data (128 samples, 5 clients) makes federation benefits hard to measure
Only binary tasks with PCA to 10 features and angle encoding
Non-IID data, client drop-out, number of clients not studied
Federated PCA emulated centrally; privacy not examined
Depth saturation beyond 5-6 layers undercuts value of deeper circuits
Error-awareness not evaluated in training; all training noiseless, no noisy simulation
Hardware results on 100 test points, no repeated runs or confidence intervals
Hardware shows deeper circuits hurt on noisy devices, contradicting premise
Hardware runs only Funnel design; Layerwise and Ancilla/Blocking not run
Gradient-norm/barren-plateau claims weakly supported, trivial locality effect, overclaimed
Gradient figure: one task, one baseline, no seed variance
Ancilla/Blocking not equivalent to Layerwise; training validity only hypothesized
Shot-efficiency claims never quantified; no shot counts or finite-shot training
Blocking design only theoretical; Funnel's Hilbert space restriction cost unmeasured
Capacity framing and Tables 2/7 confusing
Classifier count (L-1) inconsistent with layer count elsewhere
12.4% average not reproducible; 'up to' vs 'on average' used inconsistently
No theoretical convergence or aggregation analysis
Circular averaging of angles not justified
Classical heterogeneous-FL and early-exit methods dismissed rather than evaluated
Evaluation only binary classification, no multiclass
Only simple MNIST/Fashion-MNIST; needs harder or quantum-native datasets to show generality
No convergence theory or analysis of KL coupling effect on optimization
Data encoding pipeline (PCA, reupload schedule) under-specified in main text
Baselines weak (shallow vanilla, standalone, self-implemented Q-HeteroFL), inflating gains
Method appears limited to binary classification
Unclear how ansatz enables single-shot outputs from all layers
No classical baseline compared
Experimental gains seem very limited
Scalability not studied
Results limited to basic classification tasks
Approach heuristic; no convergence or bias-variance analysis of partial aggregation
Fairness gaps from seldom-updated layers not quantified or mitigated
No comparison with communication-efficient FL methods (FedDrop, STC)
Limited ablation on importance metric and hyperparameter sensitivity
